---
title: "Reproduce the site"
description: >-
  How to build this site and re-run every lesson on your own machine.
---

Every listing, figure, and proof on this site comes from code in the
repository. One command rebuilds all of it, so you can check any claim a
lesson makes.

## What you need

A computer running macOS or Linux, with about 11 GB of free disk space for
the Lean toolchain and the Mathlib build cache, and an internet connection
for the first run. You need these tools:

- Git
- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/), which
  installs the pinned Python, the Python packages, and Quarto
- [elan](https://lean-lang.org/install/manual/), which installs the pinned
  Lean toolchain
- jq 1.6 or later

## Steps

```bash
git clone https://github.com/taspinar/physics-by-construction.git
cd physics-by-construction
uv sync --locked
uv run --locked playwright install --only-shell chromium
./scripts/preflight.sh
./scripts/verify.sh
```

On Linux, the browser build needs system libraries. Add `--with-deps` to the
`playwright install` command to install them on the distributions Playwright
supports; it asks for administrator rights.

`./scripts/preflight.sh` lists every missing prerequisite with a hint to fix
it, and needs nothing beyond the tools above. `./scripts/verify.sh` runs that
check first, then runs the tests, builds every Lean proof, builds the site,
and checks the built pages. The first run downloads the Lean toolchain and
the Mathlib build cache and takes the longest. Open `site/_site/index.html`
in a browser to read the result.

The repository also has `./scripts/doctor.sh`, for the people who maintain
the site. It checks the tools of their workflow as well, such as a GitHub
account that can push to the repository, and reports them as failures when
they are absent. Rebuilding the site does not need them.

The
[development guide](https://github.com/taspinar/physics-by-construction/blob/main/docs/development.md)
has the full setup, including the commands for each tool on each system.

## Running one lesson

Each lesson's code is in `src/pbc/`, with its tests in `tests/unit/`. To run
the tests of the code that the lessons use:

```bash
uv run --locked pytest tests/unit
```

The lesson on agents records a run made with a language model. You can check
that record without a model and without a key: the build recomputes every
tool result in it. Running the agent yourself needs your own API key, as the
lesson explains.
